## How to use this document

This is a **Quarto document**. It mixes regular text (like this) with **code chunks** (the gray boxes). You can run code three ways:

| To run | Do this |
|---|---|
| One line | Put your cursor on the line and press **Command + Enter** (Mac) or **Control + Enter** (Windows) |
| A whole chunk | Click the green ▶ arrow in the top right corner of the chunk |
| The whole document | Click **Render** at the top of this panel. This makes a web page (HTML) of your work. |

When you see `____` (a blank), replace it with your own code. Type your answers to the **Questions** in the space below each one, as regular text.

The data are readings every 10 minutes from October 9 to October 23, 2026, recorded by the tank's Apex controller. See the `README.md` file for what each column means.

## Part 1: Load packages and data

Packages are add-ons that give R extra tools. You only install them once, but you load them with `library()` every time you open R. If you have not installed the tidyverse yet, run `install.packages("tidyverse")` once in the **Console** (bottom left), not in this document.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
```

Next, read the tank data into R and store it as an object called `tank`. The arrow `<-` means "save the thing on the right under the name on the left."

The `../` means "go up one folder." This document lives in the `scripts` folder, so R has to go up one level to find the `data` folder.

```{r}
tank <- read_csv("../data/tank_data.csv")
```

## Part 4: Your first plot

`ggplot` builds plots in layers:

- `ggplot(data, aes(x = ..., y = ...))` says **what** to plot
- `+ geom_line()` says **how** to draw it

```{r}
ggplot(tank, aes(x = datetime, y = temperature)) +
  geom_line()
```

Make it nicer with labels:

```{r}
ggplot(tank, aes(x = datetime, y = temperature)) +
  geom_line(color = "steelblue") +
  labs(x = "Date",
       y = "Temperature (degrees Fahrenheit)",
       title = "Stier Lab tank temperature") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Part 5: Tank detective

Something unusual happened in the tank around October 21 and 22. Look back at your temperature plot. Do you see it?

Some background on how the tank is set up:

- The **display tank** (where the corals live) holds the **heater**.
- The **sump** (the tank underneath) holds the **temperature probe**.
- The **return pump** pushes water from the sump up to the display, and the water drains back down into the sump. When the pump stops, the two tanks stop mixing.

Plot how much power the return pump used:

```{r}
ggplot(tank, aes(x = datetime, y = return_pump_watts)) +
  geom_line() +
  theme_minimal()
```

### Question 4

What happened to the return pump? Roughly when did it stop and start again?

## Part 6: Day and night

The `hour` column tells you the hour of the day (0 is midnight, 13 is 1 p.m.). This plots every light reading by hour of the day:

```{r}
ggplot(tank, aes(x = hour, y = light_watts)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2) +
  theme_minimal()
```

### Question 7

When do the lights turn on and off? When are they brightest?

**Answer:**
